(2) The scene cuts to a close-up of her face as she continues her explanation, emphasizing points with hand gestures against a dark, softly lit background. (3) A macro visual of a person's forehead is shown, highlighting enlarged pores and skin texture under bright light. (4) The doctor appears again, pointing to her own forehead and temple area to indicate specific zones of concern on the skin. (5) A microscopic image of a Demodex mite moving on a skin surface is displayed to illustrate the biological cause being discussed. (6) The doctor uses her fingers to frame her eyes and nose, demonstrating the 'normal' zone for pores as per clinical standards. (7) A split-screen or graphic overlay shows a human face model with highlighted areas differentiating normal and abnormal pore distribution. (8) The camera captures her in a side profile as she points to her cheek area, explaining oil production and skin fiberization. (9) She moves extremely close to the camera, simulating a direct patient examination, showing her eyes and nose in a macro close-up. (10) The final phase shows a clean white background with the clinic logo, LINE ID, phone number, and address information appearing sequentially.
